subject: physics_2
question_text: Under what conditions is the current through the mixed grouping of cells maximum?

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Transcribed verbatim from the book (p28, VSAQ 19). Hand-checked: with m rows in parallel and n cells in series per row, I = mnε/(mR + nr); for a fixed total number of cells mn the denominator is least when mR = nr, that is R = nr/m — the same condition the book prints. The symbols n and m are defined on the card because the book prints nr/m without saying which is which.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The condition in words
lines: In a mixed grouping the cells are arranged in
m parallel rows, with n cells in series in
The current in the circuit is maximum when
the external resistance is equal to the total
steps.margin_note: First mark. State the equality in words before writing any symbols.
steps.why: The current is mnε/(mR + nr). With the number of cells fixed, the current is largest when the denominator is least, and that happens when mR and nr are equal.
common_mistakes: Saying the internal resistance must be as small as possible. The condition is an equality, not a minimum.

recall.must_convey: That the current is maximum when the external resistance equals the total internal resistance of the battery.
accept: external resistance equals total internal resistance
R equals the internal resistance of the battery
when the two resistances are equal

steps.label: The condition in symbols
lines: Each cell has emf ε and internal resistance r.
The n cells of a row give nr, and the m rows
in parallel divide it by m:

lines.text: Current is maximum when R = nr/m

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write nr/m and say that n counts cells in a row and m counts rows.
steps.why: Cells in series add their internal resistances, giving nr for one row; m such rows in parallel divide that by m. Substituting R = nr/m gives the largest current, I = nε/2R.
common_mistakes: Writing mr/n. The n cells in series come first, then the m rows divide.

recall.must_convey: That the total internal resistance is n r by m and the current is maximum when R equals it.
accept: R equals n r by m
n cells in a row m rows in parallel

steps.memory_tip: Series first, parallel second: n multiplies r, then m divides it.

insider_note: The book prints nr/m without saying what n and m stand for. Define them in one line and the second mark is safe.
